title: Revalidation evidence — the value of pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; software-analysis DEC-001 point 7): executed results that confirm or refute an analysis artefact at a commit — a test run against a use case, a trace through a journey. This capability runs nothing: the results arrive from a capability that runs them, or from the project's own filler file. One entry per artefact and commit, keyed by the pair: its `id` is `<artefact>@<commit>`. The point is `union`, no default takes part, and its inert policy is `fallback`, because the evidence advises: a revalidation record copies the entries it draws on as support for an artefact's outcome and never in place of one, and only a revalidation or a deferral recorded on the artefact clears friction (COR-050). It reads alone, since two providers of the point are compared by this file alone (COR-053 point 5): its `$defs` carry copies of `analysis.schema.json`'s id, commit and text definitions, their one home, and a test holds each copy equal to its source. The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

evidence.description: The result of one executed check, for one artefact at one commit.

id.description: The entry's key, the pair it is for: `<artefact>@<commit>`, exactly the entry's own `artefact` and `commit` joined by `@`. A schema cannot compare two fields, so software-analysis' check holds a revalidation record's copy of an entry to it. A record finds the entry by it.

artefact.description: The artefact the run confirms or refutes.

commit.description: The commit the run was made against: the version of the system the result is true of, by its full name.

result.description: `passed`: the run did what the artefact describes — support for `holds`. `failed`: it did not — a regression with proof attached, or a sign the analysis is stale; the revalidation decides which (DEC-001 points 5 and 7).

ran.description: What was run, so a person can find it and run it again: a test by its name (`tests/test_run.py::test_sandbox`), a trace, a scripted walk through a journey.

steps.description: The steps and variants the run went through, by their numbers and letters (`2`, `2a`). They are cited, which is why they are never renumbered (DEC-001 point 3).

where.description: Where the result can be read: a pipeline run, a report file.

by.description: Who or what ran it: a capability, a pipeline, a person.

actor-id.description: An actor's id: `ACT-` and a slug, stable across renames; the key of its entry in the actors' collection file.

term-id.description: A glossary term's id: `TERM-` and a slug, separate from the term's display name, so a rename breaks nothing that cites it; the key of its entry in the glossary.

use-case-id.description: A use case's id: `UC-` and its number within the project, independent of any grouping by area — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000 (`UC-007`), and no leading zero from 1000 on (`UC-1000`), so each number has one spelling and `UC-0007` is never a second id for `UC-007`.

journey-id.description: A journey's id: `JRN-` and its number within the project — three digits, zero-padded, below 1000, and no leading zero from 1000 on, so each number has one spelling.

artefact-id.description: The id of any analysis artefact.

commit.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal name in lower case: 40 digits under SHA-1, 64 under SHA-256. An abbreviated name is refused, so a commit has one spelling and a citation matches an entry exactly.

evidence-id.description: The id of an entry of the evidence point, `pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence` (DEC-001 point 7): the artefact and the commit the result is for, `<artefact>@<commit>` — an artefact id as above, then a commit's full name. A pattern cannot refer to another, so this one spells the four id shapes and the commit again, here beside them; a test holds them in step.
